title: Lavender hydrosol analysis using UV spectroscopy and PLS regression
author: Preiner, Tarcsay, et al.
materials: Our goal was to define the main EO components and their concentrations within the hydrosol. The original samples were tenfold diluted. 0.1 ml of the sample was measured using an automatic pipette which was transferred to a 10 cm3 standard flask and filled to mark. The cuvette was filled with the examined samples and their spectra was taken with Thermo Scientific Genesys 150 UV–Vis spectrophotometer. The blank solutions were distilled water for the hydrosol samples and pentane, diethyl ether and heptane for the extracts. The spectra were taken between 200 and 600 nm range wavelengths. The main differences were seen in the UV domain between 200 and 400 nm. The spectrum of different hydrosols and distilled water (DW) can be seen on Fig. 1.Fig. 1UV–Vis spectrum of distilled water (DW) and lavender hydrosols of samples S19-S22.Fig. 1

steps.title: Prepare lavender hydrosol sample
steps.instruction: Dry lavender plant material until constant mass, chop to uniform size, steam‑distill 170 g of material using the same steam flowrate for each run to obtain the hydrosol (22 samples labelled S1‑S22).

steps.title: Dilute hydrosol tenfold
steps.instruction: Pipette 0.1 mL of the hydrosol with an automatic pipette into a 10 mL (10 cm³) standard flask and fill to the mark with distilled water; mix to obtain a ten‑fold diluted sample.

steps.title: Record UV‑Vis spectra
steps.instruction: Transfer the diluted sample to a cuvette and record its spectrum on a Thermo Scientific Genesys 150 UV‑Vis spectrophotometer from 200 nm to 600 nm; use distilled water as blank for hydrosol samples (and pentane, diethyl‑ether or heptane as blanks for extracts). Correct the spectra by subtracting the water blank and read the absorbance at the maximum change wavelength of 278 nm.

steps.title: Extract hydrosol with solvent
steps.instruction: For each solvent (heptane, pentane, diethyl‑ether) place 50 mL (50 cm³) of hydrosol in a separation funnel, add 10 mL (10 cm³) of the solvent, shake and allow the phases to contact for 10 min, then separate the layers. Perform five successive extractions with fresh heptane (five stages); perform a single extraction with pentane and with diethyl‑ether (one stage each). If the extract is too concentrated for UV‑Vis, dilute it tenfold or more.

steps.title: Measure extract UV‑Vis
steps.instruction: Record the UV‑Vis spectrum of each solvent extract under the same conditions as the hydrosol (200‑600 nm, blank with the corresponding solvent, absorbance read at 278 nm).

steps.title: Analyze extracts by GC‑MS
steps.instruction: Inject 0.1 µL of each undiluted extract into an Agilent 5975C GC‑MS equipped with an HP‑5 column (30.0 m × 0.25 mm, film thickness 0.25 µm). Set injector and detector temperatures to 250 °C. Program the oven at a heating rate of 10 °C min⁻¹ from 50 °C to 250 °C. Identify the nine main EO components (α‑pinene, β‑trans‑ocimene, β‑cis‑ocimene, linalool, octen‑1‑ol, camphor, terpinen‑4‑ol, hexyl butyrate, lavandulyl acetate).
